prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for all specific kinds of change (adoption/notification, choose_path/hint, home/new_flow, sign_in/incentive) because each has only been tested once.
Predictions were consistently too high across all tests compared to measured and noise-corrected results.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, notification: -1.6% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, hint: +2.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, new_flow: -0.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, incentive: +1.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.8%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 18.0%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [sign_in, reorder] Move sign-in after pet adoption: Move the sign-in screen to after pet selection and adoption certificates so users customize their pet before creating an account. (why: Adoption conversion is low (60.9%) and sign_in has drop-off; placing sign-in after adoption leverages user investment in their pet.)
1: [finish, new_screen] Interactive pet controls quickstart guide: Add a visual controls guide screen at the finish step demonstrating how to drag, right-click, hide, and talk to your pet on desktop. (why: Support receives multiple complaints about users not knowing how to control or talk to the pet after onboarding, and finish step median time is 395s.)
2: [home, new_flow] Animated waiting screen mini-game flow: Insert an interactive treat-tossing mini-game screen while background pet generation completes. (why: The waiting stage takes median 201s / mean 2336s, causing user drop-off while waiting for pet assets to load.)
3: [finish, copy] Desktop placement instruction on finish intro: Update the home intro text to explain exactly where the pet will land on screen and how to wake it up. (why: 3 support emails noted pet not showing up on desktop, and the finish step conversion is 64.8% with mean time over 5800s.)
4: [home, wait_info] Tip carousel and progress percentage bar on waiting screen: Show an active progress percentage bar and rotating feature tips on the waiting screen. (why: Waiting step takes median 201s / mean 2336s, leading users to believe the application froze.)
5: [choose_path, layout] Two-column choice overview layout for onboarding path: Switch choose_path screen to a two-column comparison layout side-by-side. (why: Choose path takes mean 514s and drops 23.2% of users; side-by-side options speed up decision making.)
6: [home, notification] Background system tray notification option on waiting screen: Enable desktop tray notifications so users can minimize the app during pet generation. (why: Pet generation wait mean time is 2336s; users tab away and forget to return to complete setup.)

scores.note: Targets high drop-off steps (adoption 60.9%, sign_in 72.9%), but requires flow restructuring.
Finish step loses 35.2% and support mails confirm user confusion; requires a new screen.
Addresses long wait time, but new_flow tests previously showed negative lift (-0.9%).
Directly supported by 3 support emails and finish metrics; cheap text-only change.
Directly targets high home wait time (median 201s) with low-overhead UI components.
Modest drop-off step (23.2%); choose_path tweaks previously showed positive lift (+2.5%).
